import FormalConjecturesUtil
import FormalConjectures.ErdosProblems.«510»

/-!
# Ben Green's Open Problem 81

Let $A$ be a set of size $n$ integers. Is there some absolute constant $c > 0$ and $\theta$
such that $\sum_{a \in A} \cos(a \theta) \leq - c \sqrt{n}$?

*References:*
- [Ben Green's Open Problem 81](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#section.11)
- [erdosproblems.com/510](https://www.erdosproblems.com/510)

This file points to the canonical formalization in `FormalConjectures.ErdosProblems.«510»`.
-/

reformulations.difference: The canonical theorem imported by this file uses a strict inequality for all sufficiently large cardinalities, whereas Green phrases the question with a non-strict inequality without an explicit large-cardinality qualification.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For every nonempty finite set A of positive integers, its cosine sum f has minimum at most -1/2. Indeed, with normalized integration over a period, ∫f=0, ∫f²=|A|/2, and f≤|A|; integrating (f-min f)(|A|-f)≥0 gives min f≤-1/2. This uniform bound covers the finitely many omitted cardinalities after decreasing the absolute constant. Conversely, a non-strict square-root bound becomes strict for every positive cardinality by halving the constant. The empty-set case of Green’s non-strict inequality is automatic. Thus the two versions pose the same question.

sources_consulted: https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#section.11 — Problem 81, its comments and 2025 update, and the associated bibliography.

https://www.erdosproblems.com/510 — read through https://r.jina.ai/https://www.erdosproblems.com/510 because direct requests encountered Cloudflare; the page identifies this with Green 81 and records it as open.
https://arxiv.org/e-print/2509.05260 — Bedert, Polynomial bounds for the Chowla Cosine Problem, v3 LaTeX source: Introduction, Theorem 1.1, and preliminary observations.
https://eudml.org/doc/278427 — bibliographic record for Ruzsa, Negative values of cosine sums. The linked publisher PDF was unavailable; the bound is also stated explicitly in Bedert’s introduction.
review.notes: The reviewed file introduces no mathematical declarations or status attributes; it imports the canonical Erdős 510 module. I checked that module’s main theorem and both cited variants to verify the pointer. Bedert explicitly specifies positive integers, supporting the canonical restriction 0 ∉ A despite Green’s abbreviated wording. His current stronger bound also implies the recorded N^(1/7) variant. Scratch checks compiled successfully, covering admissible sets at every cardinality, empty and singleton cases, the atTop threshold, strict-bound adjustment, and real-power boundary values.
